agent_notes: The Ketiv is לְמַעֲנִיתָם in the written text, with the apparatus marking (Q(K)); the packet gives the form lema'anotam. I glossed the plain sense 'to/for their furrows'. The Ketiv/Qere difference is a matter of vowel/spelling and does not change the sense. The Hebrew 'furrows' (מַעֲנָה) occurs elsewhere only in 1 Sam 14:14, where it is a measure of ploughland; Rashi, Ibn Ezra and Radak all point to it or explain it as the furrow-line.

BBE's 'long were the wounds they made' reads the furrows as the wounds on the back. The Hebrew says furrows only, and the wound image is the reader's inference; I kept the furrow in the literal layer and let the dramatic layer draw out the wound.

agent_notes: The question whether the closing blessing is part of the simile (the passers-by do not greet the withered grass) or reports a harvest custom as the foil is clear in the commentary of Radak, Metzudat David and Meiri. I followed that reading. Boaz's greeting in Ruth 2:4 is the cited parallel (Radak, Meiri).
